picks.editorial_note: Stony Brook mathematician James Glimm discusses OpenAI's reported solution to the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem, one of the seven Clay Millennium Prize problems — a landmark claim that AI can crack century-old open questions in pure mathematics.
picks.title: Solving for Tomorrow: James Glimm on Mathematics, AI and Life

picks.editorial_note: An international team including Science Tokyo built a protein language model unifying sequence and 3D structure data, advancing the ability to map evolutionary relationships across the entire protein universe — a foundational tool for biology and drug design.
picks.title: Uniting sequence and structure to map the protein universe | Science Tokyo

picks.editorial_note: UCLA researchers' 'physical AI' approach uses self-organized nanowire/nanoparticle networks as hardware-based neural networks, pointing toward radically more energy-efficient, locally-processed AI at the edge.
picks.title: Toward physical AI: When the hardware becomes the neural network

picks.editorial_note: The UK's AI Minister marked a construction milestone on the country's most powerful supercomputer at Edinburgh, a major government-university investment intended to power drug discovery and climate research.
picks.title: AI Minister marks milestone on Supercomputer build | News | The University of Edinburgh

picks.editorial_note: France committed €13.5 million to launch a national AI Evaluation Program at Inria, building scientific methods to assess AI safety, robustness and vulnerabilities — a concrete step toward government-backed AI safety infrastructure.
picks.title: France 2030 | Launch of the AI Evaluation Program: a scientific roadmap for the evaluation and safety of artificial intelligence

picks.editorial_note: Edinburgh's Genome Foundry secured a three-year government-backed partnership with ARIA to scale up AI- and robotics-driven biofoundry capabilities, linking frontier AI to synthetic biology infrastructure.
picks.title: Funding boost transforms AI-enabled biological research | News | The University of Edinburgh

picks.editorial_note: A $5 million NSF award to ASU, San Diego State, and the University of Utah will build PARAPET, a national cyberinfrastructure for privacy-preserving data sharing across institutions — significant federal investment in trustworthy AI infrastructure.
picks.title: $5M NSF award to enhance data protections for users nationwide

picks.editorial_note: Imperial College London biosecurity experts warned about AI's dual-use risks in pathogen design ahead of a UN biosecurity summit, spotlighting a policy debate with direct implications for AI governance.
picks.title: AI, pandemics and food security: Imperial experts discuss the future of biosecurity

picks.editorial_note: UCLA's chief AI officer joined global discussion of AI safety as King Charles hosted an international AI summit with tech leaders, underscoring growing head-of-state engagement in AI governance.
picks.title: King Charles hosts AI summit — and more UCLA media

picks.editorial_note: SRI International won a role in a U.S.-Korea defense collaboration to build an autonomous Space Domain Awareness payload, extending AI-driven autonomy into allied space defense infrastructure.
picks.title: SRI wins autonomous Space Domain Awareness role in U.S.–Korea collaboration - SRI
